02

Decision routes

Choose one outcome from several and combine related conditions accurately.

01

Several routes

Use elif between the first if and final else.

if score >= 80:
    band = "Gold"
elif score >= 60:
    band = "Silver"
else:
    band = "Bronze"
02

Logical AND

The whole condition is True only when both comparisons are True.

if age >= 14 and consent == "yes":
    print("Eligible")
03

Logical OR and NOT

or needs one True condition. not reverses a Boolean result.

if member == "yes" or code == "SAVE":
    print("Discount")
Order is part of the algorithm

Python stops at the first True route in an if/elif/else structure. A correct condition in the wrong position can still create a logic error.

    PYTHON LAB REFERENCE
    Support & examples
    Use this reference to check multi-way decisions, logical operators and the order of routes. None of the examples solves a build task.
    Key concepts
    • Use if/elif/else when one route must be chosen from several.
    • Python checks routes from top to bottom and stops at the first True condition.
    • and requires both conditions; or requires at least one; not reverses a Boolean.
    • Place the most restrictive or highest boundary first when using descending bands.
    • Use a final else to catch all remaining valid values.
    Common errors
    • Putting a broad condition before a more specific condition
    • Writing else with a condition
    • Repeating if when the routes should be mutually exclusive
    • Forgetting that and/or conditions still need complete comparisons on both sides
    Misconceptions to avoid
    Misconception: elif checks every route
    Once a route is True, Python skips the remaining elif and else blocks.
    Misconception: x == 5 or 6 checks for either value
    Write x == 5 or x == 6. Each side of or must be a complete Boolean expression.
    Misconception: and and or mean the same thing
    and is stricter because every condition must be True; or accepts any one True condition.
    EXAMPLE 01 · ORDERED BANDS
    Parcel label
    weight = float(input("Weight in kg: "))

if weight > 20:
    print("Heavy")
elif weight > 5:
    print("Standard")
else:
    print("Light")
    The highest boundary is checked first so a 25 kg parcel cannot enter the Standard route.
    EXAMPLE 02 · AND
    Sports hall entry
    age = int(input("Age: "))
induction = input("Induction complete? yes/no: ")

if age >= 16 and induction == "yes":
    print("Entry permitted")
else:
    print("See a member of staff")
    Both comparisons must be True for entry to be permitted.
    EXAMPLE 03 · OR
    Voucher route
    member = input("Member? yes/no: ")
code = input("Voucher code: ")

if member == "yes" or code == "SAVE5":
    print("Discount available")
else:
    print("Standard price")
    Either route can make the whole condition True.
